python3 << 'EOF'
# The spurious pairing cascades: each unit's G-rich stems pair with adjacent units' C-rich stems.
# The structure has GGGC...GCCG patterns. The unit sequence (stems G, loops U):
# unit: UGGGUGGGUGGUUUUCCGGUUUUCCUCCCU
# opens: GGG UGG UGG, loop1 UUUU, close CCGG, loop2 UUUU, close CCGG, then CCC outer close
# Problem: adjacent units stack so the CCC close of one + GGG open of next forms long helix.
# The four units sit between the same outer helix (5-8 / 113-110). The internal units share
# the long region 9-114. The spurious pairs form across units.
# 
# Key insight: the target has the 4 units inside one big outer helix (5-8 ... 110-113).
# Between units there's NO separator - unit1 close (positions 31-33) directly followed by
# unit2 open (35-37) with only pos 34 as '.'.
# So we get ...CCC G... pattern -> pairs (33,35) etc? No, (32,35) wait spurious (33,61) etc.
#
# Actually spurious (33,61): pos33 is ')' closing outer of u1, pos61 '(' opening s1 of u3.
# These shouldn't pair if non-complementary.
#
# Better approach: make loops A-rich (not U), and make stem closing bases non-adjacent-complementary.
# Let me think about the unit's sequence layout more carefully and design each unit with
# distinct stem sequences so cross-unit pairing is minimized.
#
# Actually, the fundamental issue: when all 4 units use identical G...C stems, the GGG of unit2
# can pair with CCC of unit4 etc. We need EACH unit's stems to use different base identities.
#
# Let me design with alternating: unit1 stems GGG/CCC, unit2 stems CCC/GGG, etc. But then
# the close of unit1 (CCC) is adjacent to open of unit2 (CCC) - both C, won't pair. Good.
# But unit2 close (GGG) adjacent unit3 open (GGG) - won't pair. 
# However unit2 open CCC could pair with unit4 close GGG if they're brought together...
# Actually in the target, unit1-4 are arranged linearly inside the outer helix.
# Positions: u1=10-33, u2=35-58, u3=60-83, u4=85-108.
# In the folded target, these are independent hairpin loops hanging off the outer helix.
# But if stems are complementary across units, alternative folds form.
#
# Strategy: make each unit's stem sequences unique and non-cross-complementary.
# Use 4 different "codes":
# u1: outer=GGC/CGGclose, s1=GA/UC, s2=AG/CU  (but need watson-crick: open G close C, etc.)
# Let me just assign per-unit stem bases from a 4-letter rotation ensuring no two adjacent units
# have reverse-complement relationship.
#
# Simpler: use A-U for the WEAK 2bp s1/s2 helices (they're only 2bp, AU might suffice and
# avoids strong cross-pairing), and G-C for the 3bp outer and 4bp outermost.
target='.....((((.(((.((....))((....)).))).(((.((....))((....)).))).(((.((....))((....)).))).(((.((....))((....)).))).)))).....'
st=[];pairs={}
for i,c in enumerate(target):
    if c=='(':st.append(i)
    elif c==')':
        j=st.pop();pairs[j]=i;pairs[i]=j
seq=['A']*len(target)
# outermost 4bp (5-8 / 110-113): GC
for i,j in [(5,113),(6,112),(7,111),(8,110)]:
    seq[i]='G';seq[j]='C'
# each unit outer 3bp: GC; s1 2bp: AU; s2 2bp: AU
units={
 'u1':{'outer_open':[10,11,12],'outer_close':[33,32,31],'s1_open':[14,15],'s1_close':[21,20],'s2_open':[22,23],'s2_close':[29,28]},
 'u2':{'outer_open':[35,36,37],'outer_close':[58,57,56],'s1_open':[39,40],'s1_close':[46,45],'s2_open':[47,48],'s2_close':[54,53]},
 'u3':{'outer_open':[60,61,62],'outer_close':[83,82,81],'s1_open':[64,65],'s1_close':[71,70],'s2_open':[72,73],'s2_close':[79,78]},
 'u4':{'outer_open':[85,86,87],'outer_close':[108,107,106],'s1_open':[89,90],'s1_close':[96,95],'s2_open':[97,98],'s2_close':[104,103]},
}
# To break cross-unit complementarity, use different patterns per unit for the 3bp outer stem.
# But keep s1/s2 = AU for all (weak). Loops = G or C? Use A (no pairing).
# Actually for s1/s2 2bp to be stable enough alone, AU 2bp is weak (~-1kcal). GC 2bp better.
# But GC causes cross-talk. Let me try mixed: alternate per unit.
patterns={
 'u1': {'o':'GCG','s1':'GC','s2':'CG'},  # opens GCG, s1 GC, s2 CG
 'u2': {'o':'CGC','s1':'AU','s2':'UA'},
 'u3': {'o':'GCG','s1':'GC','s2':'CG'},
 'u4': {'o':'CGC','s1':'AU','s2':'UA'},
}
def comp(b):
    return {'A':'U','U':'A','G':'C','C':'G'}[b]
for u,p in patterns.items():
    oseq=p['o']; cbases=[comp(b) for b in oseq]
    for k,pos in enumerate(units[u]['outer_open']):
        seq[pos]=oseq[k]
    for k,pos in enumerate(units[u]['outer_close']):
        seq[pos]=cbases[k]
    s1o=p['s1']; s1c=[comp(b) for b in s1o]
    for k,pos in enumerate(units[u]['s1_open']):
        seq[pos]=s1o[k]
    for k,pos in enumerate(units[u]['s1_close']):
        seq[pos]=s1c[k]
    s2o=p['s2']; s2c=[comp(b) for b in s2o]
    for k,pos in enumerate(units[u]['s2_open']):
        seq[pos]=s2o[k]
    for k,pos in enumerate(units[u]['s2_close']):
        seq[pos]=s2c[k]
# verify complementarity
ok=True
for i,j in pairs.items():
    if i<j:
        pair=(seq[i],seq[j])
        if pair not in [('G','C'),('C','G'),('A','U'),('U','A'),('G','U'),('U','G')]:
            print('bad',i,j,seq[i],seq[j]);ok=False
print('ok',ok)
s=''.join(seq)
print(s);print(len(s))
EOF
